sanskrit: bhūmipradānena gatiṃ labhaty āśramasaṃmitām naṣṭasyārthasya saṃprāptiṃ kṛtvā phalam upāśnute
english: By the gift of land one attains a destiny equal to that of the hermitages of asceticism; and by restoring to a man wealth that was lost, one reaps the fruit thereof.

sanskrit: abhipretām asaṃkliṣṭāṃ kṛtvākāmavatīṃ kriyām na yāti nirayaṃ kaś cid iti dharmavido viduḥ
english: He who performs a desired deed without grudging and free of self-interest goes not to hell — so the knowers of dharma have understood.

sanskrit: nāga uvāca abhimānena māno me jātidoṣeṇa vai mahān roṣaḥ saṃkalpajaḥ sādhvi dagdho vācāgninā tvayā
english: The Nāga said: My pride was born of arrogance, and through the flaw of my birth a great wrath sprang up from my own resolve, O virtuous one — but you have burned it away with the fire of your words.

sanskrit: na ca roṣād ahaṃ sādhvi paśyeyam adhikaṃ tamaḥ yasya vaktavyatāṃ yānti viśeṣeṇa bhujaṃgamāḥ
english: And I see no greater darkness than wrath, O virtuous one — a fault to which serpents above all others are held accountable.

sanskrit: doṣasya hi vaśaṃ gatvā daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān tathā śakrapratispardhī hato rāmeṇa saṃyuge
english: For having fallen under the sway of this fault, the mighty ten-necked one, who dared to rival Śakra, was slain by Rāma in battle.

sanskrit: antaḥpuragataṃ vatsaṃ śrutvā rāmeṇa nirhṛtam dharṣaṇād roṣasaṃvignāḥ kārtavīryasutā hatāḥ
english: And hearing that Rāma had carried off the calf kept within their inner chambers, the sons of Kārtavīrya, agitated with wrath at the affront, were slain.

sanskrit: jāmadagnyena rāmeṇa sahasranayanopamaḥ saṃyuge nihato roṣāt kārtavīryo mahābalaḥ
english: By Rāma the son of Jamadagni, the mighty Kārtavīrya, peer of the thousand-eyed one, was struck down in battle through his own wrath.

sanskrit: tad eṣa tapasāṃ śatruḥ śreyasaś ca nipātanaḥ nigṛhīto mayā roṣaḥ śrutvaiva vacanaṃ tava
english: And so this wrath, the foe of austerities and the destroyer of all that is good, I have now subdued in myself the moment I heard your words.

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ ca viśeṣeṇa praśaṃsāmy anapāyini yasya me tvaṃ viśālākṣi bhāryā sarvaguṇānvitā
english: And I count myself especially blessed, O steadfast one, that you, large-eyed lady endowed with every virtue, are my wife.

sanskrit: eṣa tatraiva gacchāmi yatra tiṣṭhaty asau dvijaḥ sarvathā coktavān vākyaṃ nākṛtārthaḥ prayāsyati
english: I go now to that very place where the brāhmaṇa abides; and since he has indeed spoken his word, he shall not depart with his purpose unfulfilled.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sa pannagapatis tatra prayayau brāhmaṇaṃ prati tam eva manasā dhyāyan kāryavattāṃ vicārayan
english: Bhīṣma said: That lord of serpents set out toward the brāhmaṇa, pondering him in his mind and weighing the purpose at hand.

sanskrit: tam abhikramya nāgendro matimān sa nareśvara provāca madhuraṃ vākyaṃ prakṛtyā dharmavatsalaḥ
english: Approaching him, that wise lord of Nāgas, O ruler of men, devoted by nature to dharma, spoke these honeyed words.

sanskrit: bho bho kṣāmyābhibhāṣe tvāṃ na roṣaṃ kartum arhasi iha tvam abhisaṃprāptaḥ kasyārthe kiṃ prayojanam
english: Sir, I beg your pardon as I address you; you should bear me no anger. For whose sake have you come here, and to what end?

sanskrit: ābhimukhyād abhikramya snehāt pṛcchāmi te dvija vivikte gomatītīre kiṃ vā tvaṃ paryupāsase
english: Coming straight up to you out of affection, I ask you, O twice-born: upon this solitary bank of the Gomatī, what is it that you worship?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca dharmāraṇyaṃ hi māṃ viddhi nāgaṃ draṣṭum ihāgatam padmanābhaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ tatra me kāryam āhitam
english: The brāhmaṇa said: Know that I have come to this Dharma-forest to see the Nāga, the lotus-naveled chief of the twice-born; in him my purpose is fixed.

sanskrit: tasya cāham asāṃnidhyaṃ śrutavān asmi taṃ gatam svajanaṃ taṃ pratīkṣāmi parjanyam iva karṣakaḥ
english: But I have heard that he is absent, that he has gone away; and I await him, my own kinsman, as a farmer awaits the rain-cloud.

sanskrit: tasya cākleśakaraṇaṃ svastikārasamāhitam vartayāmy ayutaṃ brahma yogayukto nirāmayaḥ
english: To work him no trouble, intent on his welfare, I recite the sacred word ten thousand times, joined in yoga and free of affliction.

sanskrit: nāga uvāca aho kalyāṇavṛttas tvaṃ sādhu sajjanavatsalaḥ śravāḍhyas tvaṃ mahābhāga paraṃ snehena paśyasi
english: The Nāga said: Ah, you are of blessed conduct, truly devoted to the good; rich in sacred learning, O illustrious one, you look upon me with the highest affection.

sanskrit: ahaṃ sa nāgo viprarṣe yathā māṃ vindate bhavān ājñāpaya yathā svairaṃ kiṃ karomi priyaṃ tava
english: I am that very Nāga, O sage among brāhmaṇas, whom you would find; command me freely as you wish — what kindness may I do for you?

sanskrit: bhavantaṃ svajanād asmi saṃprāptaṃ śrutavān iha atas tvāṃ svayam evāhaṃ draṣṭum abhyāgato dvija
english: I have heard from my kinsfolk that you had come here, and so I myself have come forth to see you, O twice-born.

sanskrit: saṃprāptaś ca bhavān adya kṛtārthaḥ pratiyāsyati visrabdho māṃ dvijaśreṣṭha viṣaye yoktum arhasi
english: And now that you have come, today you shall return with your purpose accomplished; with full confidence, O best of the twice-born, you may set me to any task within my domain.

sanskrit: vayaṃ hi bhavatā sarve guṇakrītā viśeṣataḥ yas tvam ātmahitaṃ tyaktvā mām evehānurudhyase
english: For we are all bought over by your virtues, and above all you, who, setting aside your own advantage, are devoted here to me alone.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca āgato 'haṃ mahābhāga tava darśanalālasaḥ kaṃ cid artham anarthajñaḥ praṣṭukāmo bhujaṃgama
english: The brāhmaṇa said: I have come, O illustrious one, longing for the sight of you, wishing to ask, in my ignorance, about a certain matter, O serpent.

sanskrit: aham ātmānam ātmastho mārgamāṇo ''tmano hitam vāsārthinaṃ mahāprājña balavantam upāsmi ha
english: Established in the Self and seeking my own welfare, I approach you, O greatly wise and mighty one, as one in search of a refuge.

sanskrit: prakāśitas tvaṃ svaguṇair yaśogarbhagabhastibhiḥ śaśāṅkakarasaṃsparśair hṛdyair ātmaprakāśitaiḥ
english: You are made radiant by your own virtues, whose rays are pregnant with glory, soothing as the touch of the moon's beams, delightful, shining from within.

sanskrit: tasya me praśnam utpannaṃ chindhi tvam anilāśana paścāt kāryaṃ vadiṣyāmi śrotum arhati me bhavān
english: Resolve, then, the question that has arisen in me, O eater of wind; afterward I shall tell you my errand, and you should hear me out.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca vivasvato gacchati paryayeṇa; voḍhuṃ bhavāṃs taṃ ratham ekacakram āścaryabhūtaṃ yadi tatra kiṃ cid; dṛṣṭaṃ tvayā śaṃsitum arhasi tvam
english: The brāhmaṇa said: Since you in your turn go forth to bear that single-wheeled, wondrous chariot of Vivasvat — if you have seen anything remarkable there, you should relate it.

sanskrit: nāga uvāca yasya raśmisahasreṣu śākhāsv iva vihaṃgamāḥ vasanty āśritya munayaḥ saṃsiddhā daivataiḥ saha
english: The Nāga said: Upon whose thousand rays, as birds upon branches, perfected sages dwell, taking refuge there together with the gods —

sanskrit: yato vāyur viniḥsṛtya sūryaraśmyāśrito mahān vijṛmbhaty ambare vipra kim āścaryataraṃ tataḥ
english: From whom the mighty wind, issuing forth and resting upon the sun's rays, spreads wide across the sky, O brāhmaṇa — what is more wondrous than that?

sanskrit: śukro nāmāsitaḥ pādo yasya vāridharo 'mbare toyaṃ sṛjati varṣāsu kim āścaryam ataḥ param
english: Whose dark ray, named Śukra, becomes a cloud-bearer in the sky and pours forth water in the rains — what is more wondrous than that?

sanskrit: yo 'ṣṭamāsāṃs tu śucinā kiraṇenojjhitaṃ payaḥ paryādatte punaḥ kāle kim āścaryam ataḥ param
english: Who for eight months draws up the waters shed by his radiant beam, and again gives them back in their season — what is more wondrous than that?

sanskrit: yasya tejoviśeṣeṣu nityam ātmā pratiṣṭhitaḥ yato bījaṃ mahī ceyaṃ dhāryate sacarācaram
english: In whose particular splendors the Self is forever established, and from whom the seed of life and this earth with all that moves and is still are upheld —

sanskrit: yatra devo mahābāhuḥ śāśvataḥ paramo 'kṣaraḥ anādinidhano vipra kim āścaryam ataḥ param
english: In whom abides the mighty-armed god, eternal, supreme, imperishable, without beginning or end, O brāhmaṇa — what is more wondrous than that?

sanskrit: āścaryāṇām ivāścaryam idam ekaṃ tu me śṛṇu vimale yan mayā dṛṣṭam ambare sūryasaṃśrayāt
english: Yet hear from me this one thing, a wonder among wonders, which I beheld in the clear sky while attending upon the Sun.

sanskrit: purā madhyāhnasamaye lokāṃs tapati bhāskare pratyādityapratīkāśaḥ sarvataḥ pratyadṛśyata
english: Once at the hour of noon, while the maker of light was scorching the worlds, there appeared from every side a being resembling a second sun set against the sun.

sanskrit: sa lokāṃs tejasā sarvān svabhāsā nirvibhāsayan ādityābhimukho 'bhyeti gaganaṃ pāṭayann iva
english: Lighting up all the worlds with his radiance, with his own splendor, he advanced toward the sun, as if cleaving the heavens apart.

sanskrit: hutāhutir iva jyotir vyāpya tejomarīcibhiḥ anirdeśyena rūpeṇa dvitīya iva bhāskaraḥ
english: Like a flame fed with offered oblation, pervading all with the rays of his brilliance, in a form beyond describing, he seemed a second sun.

sanskrit: tasyābhigamanaprāptau hasto datto vivasvatā tenāpi dakṣiṇo hasto dattaḥ pratyarcanārthinā
english: As he drew near and arrived, Vivasvat extended his hand to him, and he too, seeking to return the homage, extended his right hand.

sanskrit: tato bhittvaiva gaganaṃ praviṣṭo ravimaṇḍalam ekībhūtaṃ ca tat tejaḥ kṣaṇenādityatāṃ gatam
english: Then, cleaving the very sky, he entered the orb of the sun; and that splendor, made one, in an instant attained the nature of the sun itself.

sanskrit: tatra naḥ saṃśayo jātas tayos tejaḥsamāgame anayoḥ ko bhavet sūryo rathastho yo 'yam āgataḥ
english: Thereupon a doubt arose in us at the meeting of those two splendors: which of the two is the Sun — this one stationed in the chariot, or that one who has come?

sanskrit: te vayaṃ jātasaṃdehāḥ paryapṛcchāmahe ravim ka eṣa divam ākramya gataḥ sūrya ivāparaḥ
english: And we, our doubt thus arisen, questioned the Sun: who is this that has mounted the heavens and passed on, like a second sun?

sanskrit: sūrya uvāca naiṣa devo 'nilasakho nāsuro na ca pannagaḥ uñchavṛttivrate siddho munir eṣa divaṃ gataḥ
english: The Sun said: This is no god, no friend of the wind, no Asura, nor any serpent; it is a sage, perfected in the vow of gleaning his livelihood, who has thus ascended to heaven.

sanskrit: eṣa mūlaphalāhāraḥ śīrṇaparṇāśanas tathā abbhakṣo vāyubhakṣaś ca āsīd vipraḥ samāhitaḥ
english: This brāhmaṇa, living on roots and fruits, eating fallen leaves, feeding on water and on air, abode in deep self-restraint.

sanskrit: ṛcaś cānena vipreṇa saṃhitāntarabhiṣṭutāḥ svargadvārakṛtodyogo yenāsau tridivaṃ gataḥ
english: By this brāhmaṇa were the sacred verses chanted, hidden within their collected texts; by such effort, with heaven's gate as his goal, he has gone to the triple heaven.

sanskrit: asannadhīranākāṅkṣī nityam uñchaśilāśanaḥ sarvabhūtahite yukta eṣa vipro bhujaṃgama
english: Steadfast and without craving, ever subsisting on gleaned and gathered grain, devoted to the welfare of all beings — such is this brāhmaṇa, O serpent.

sanskrit: na hi devā na gandharvā nāsurā na ca pannagāḥ prabhavantīha bhūtānāṃ prāptānāṃ paramāṃ gatim
english: For neither gods nor Gandharvas, neither Asuras nor serpents, prevail here over those beings who have attained the supreme goal.

sanskrit: nāga uvāca etad evaṃvidhaṃ dṛṣṭam āścaryaṃ tatra me dvija saṃsiddho mānuṣaḥ kāyo yo 'sau siddhagatiṃ gataḥ sūryeṇa sahito brahman pṛthivīṃ parivartate
english: The Nāga said: Such was the wonder I beheld there, O twice-born — a man's body made perfect, which, having reached the goal of the perfected, now circles the earth in company with the Sun, O brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca āścaryaṃ nātra saṃdehaḥ suprīto 'smi bhujaṃgama anvarthopagatair vākyaiḥ panthānaṃ cāsmi darśitaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa said: It is a wonder, no doubt of it; I am well pleased, O serpent, and by your words, fitting and to the point, I have been shown the path.

sanskrit: svasti te 'stu gamiṣyāmi sādho bhujagasattama smaraṇīyo 'smi bhavatā saṃpreṣaṇaniyojanaiḥ
english: May it be well with you; I shall depart, O good one, best of serpents. Keep me in remembrance, with errands and commands to fulfill.

sanskrit: nāga uvāca anuktvā madgataṃ kāryaṃ kvedānīṃ prasthito bhavān ucyatāṃ dvija yat kāryaṃ yadarthaṃ tvam ihāgataḥ
english: The Nāga said: Without telling the errand you had with me, where do you set out for now? Speak, O twice-born, what is your business, and for what purpose you have come here.

sanskrit: uktānukte kṛte kārye mām āmantrya dvijarṣabha mayā pratyabhyanujñātas tato yāsyasi brāhmaṇa
english: Whether your errand, spoken or unspoken, be done, take leave of me, O bull among the twice-born; then, with my consent given, you shall go, O brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: na hi māṃ kevalaṃ dṛṣṭvā tyaktvā praṇayavān iha gantum arhasi viprarṣe vṛkṣamūlagato yathā
english: For having merely looked upon me, you should not, affectionate as you are, leave me and go, O sage among brāhmaṇas, as one passes by a tree at whose foot one has rested.

sanskrit: tvayi cāhaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha bhavān mayi na saṃśayaḥ loko 'yaṃ bhavataḥ sarvaḥ kā cintā mayi te 'nagha
english: In you am I, O best of the twice-born, and you are in me — there is no doubt; all this world is yours. What anxiety, then, can you have concerning me, O sinless one?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca evam etan mahāprājña vijñātārtha bhujaṃgama nātiriktās tvayā devāḥ sarvathaiva yathātatham
english: The brāhmaṇa said: So it is, O greatly wise one, who has understood the truth, O serpent; not in any respect have you set the gods above what is just so.

sanskrit: ya evāhaṃ sa eva tvam evam etad bhujaṃgama ahaṃ bhavāṃś ca bhūtāni sarve sarvatragāḥ sadā
english: He who is I is the very one who is you — even so it is, O serpent; I and you and all beings are forever all-pervading.

sanskrit: āsīt tu me bhogapate saṃśayaḥ puṇyasaṃcaye so 'ham uñchavrataṃ sādho cariṣyāmy arthadarśanam
english: But I had a doubt, O lord of serpents, concerning the gathering of merit; and so I, O good one, shall practice the vow of gleaning, having now seen its purpose.

sanskrit: eṣa me niścayaḥ sādho kṛtaḥ kāraṇavattaraḥ āmantrayāmi bhadraṃ te kṛtārtho 'smi bhujaṃgama
english: This is my resolve, O good one, now firmly grounded in its reason. I take my leave of you — may it be well with you; my purpose is accomplished, O serpent.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sa cāmantryoragaśreṣṭhaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ kṛtaniścayaḥ dīkṣākāṅkṣī tadā rājaṃś cyavanaṃ bhārgavaṃ śritaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: And that brāhmaṇa, having taken leave of the best of serpents, his resolve now firm and longing for consecration, then betook himself, O king, to Cyavana of Bhṛgu's line.

sanskrit: sa tena kṛtasaṃskāro dharmam evopatasthivān tathaiva ca kathām etāṃ rājan kathitavāṃs tadā
english: By him the sacraments were performed for him, and he devoted himself wholly to dharma; and even so, O king, he related this very tale at that time.

sanskrit: bhārgaveṇāpi rājendra janakasya niveśane kathaiṣā kathitā puṇyā nāradāya mahātmane
english: And by the Bhārgava too, O lord of kings, in the dwelling of Janaka, this holy tale was told to the great-souled Nārada.

sanskrit: nāradenāpi rājendra devendrasya niveśane kathitā bharataśreṣṭha pṛṣṭenākliṣṭakarmaṇā
english: And by Nārada too, O lord of kings, in the dwelling of the lord of the gods, it was told when he was asked, O best of the Bhāratas, he of untiring deeds.

sanskrit: devarājena ca purā kathaiṣā kathitā śubhā samastebhyaḥ praśastebhyo vasubhyo vasudhādhipa
english: And by the king of the gods of old, this auspicious tale was told to all the renowned Vasus together, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: yadā ca mama rāmeṇa yuddham āsīt sudāruṇam vasubhiś ca tadā rājan katheyaṃ kathitā mama
english: And when I had that most terrible battle with Rāma, then, O king, this tale was told to me by the Vasus.

sanskrit: pṛcchamānāya tattvena mayā tubhyaṃ viśāṃ pate katheyaṃ kathitā puṇyā dharmyā dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: And to you, who ask of it in truth, O lord of peoples, I have told this holy tale, in accord with dharma, O best of the upholders of dharma.

sanskrit: tad eṣa paramo dharmo yan māṃ pṛcchasi bhārata asannadhīr anākāṅkṣī dharmārthakaraṇe nṛpa
english: This, then, is the highest dharma about which you ask me, O Bhārata: to be steadfast and without craving in the working out of dharma and its ends, O king.

sanskrit: sa ca kila kṛtaniścayo dvijāgryo; bhujagapatipratideśitārthakṛtyaḥ yamaniyamasamāhito vanāntaṃ; parigaṇitoñchaśilāśanaḥ praviṣṭaḥ
english: And that foremost of the twice-born, his resolve made firm, his course of action pointed out to him by the lord of serpents, composed in restraint and observance, subsisting on measured gleanings of gathered grain, entered the depths of the forest.
